1.title: Structured Output, Schemas, Validation and Retry
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Structured Output, Schemas, Validation and Retry. This module covers task statements four point three and four point four: structured output, validation and retry. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Why tool use with a Jason (Java Script Object Notation) schema is the most reliable way to get structured output. The tool choice modes for extraction. Schema design: required versus optional, nullable, enums with "other" and "unclear". Validation and retry with error feedback, and when retry cannot help. Syntax errors versus semantic errors, and self-check fields.

1.title: Case Check-In: Birchwood Supply Reads Supplier Invoices
1.text: Our running case is Birchwood Supply. Birchwood Supply Reads Supplier Invoices. Suppliers send invoices as P D F s, emails and scans. The system must produce clean Jason: supplier, invoice date, line items, total. Sometimes the text answer has broken Jason, and sometimes a required field is invented because the document does not contain it.

1.title: Structured Output with Tool Use
1.text: Structured Output with Tool Use. Tool use with a Jason schema is the most reliable approach for schema-compliant output: define an extraction tool whose input schema is your target structure, make Claude call it, and read the data from the tool use block's input. That removes Jason syntax errors. The three tool choice modes matter here.

1.title: Structured Output with Tool Use, continued
1.text: Structured Output with Tool Use, continued. "auto". Result: The model may return text instead of calling the tool. Use for extraction when: Not enough if you need guaranteed structure. "any". Result: The model must call a tool, but chooses which. Use for extraction when: Several extraction schemas exist (invoice, receipt, contract) and the document type is unknown. Forced {"type":"tool","name":"extract metadata"}. Result: The model must call that tool. Use for extraction when: A particular extraction must run first, before enrichment steps.

1.title: Structured Output with Tool Use, continued
1.text: Structured Output with Tool Use, continued. The figure shows this: Extraction with tool use: the model fills a schema through a tool call; tool choice any guarantees a tool call when the document type is unknown. In current A P I (application programming interface) documentation, any and forced tool are rejected (four hundred error) on some newer models and with manual extended thinking. The documented alternatives are strict: true on the tool (inputs guaranteed to match the schema) with auto, or structured outputs (output config.format with a Jason schema). The exam guide teaches tool use with "any" and forced selection; answer as the guide does. As of eight November two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: What a schema does not guarantee
1.text: What a schema does not guarantee. Examples. Syntax errors (broken Jason, wrong types, missing required keys): Unclosed brace, string instead of number. Semantic errors (valid Jason, wrong meaning): Line items do not sum to the total; a value placed in the wrong field. Tool use or strict schema. Syntax errors (broken Jason, wrong types, missing required keys): Eliminated. Semantic errors (valid Jason, wrong meaning): Not prevented. Handle with. Syntax errors (broken Jason, wrong types, missing required keys): The schema itself. Semantic errors (valid Jason, wrong meaning): Validation code and self-check fields.

1.title: Schema design rules
1.text: Schema design rules. The figure shows this: Schema design: nullable fields prevent fabrication, enums with other plus detail allow growth, unclear handles ambiguity. Make a field optional or nullable when the document may not contain it. If a field is required, the model may fabricate a value to satisfy the schema. Use enums for categories, with an "other" value plus a detail string so new categories do not break the schema.

1.title: Schema design rules, continued
1.text: Schema design rules, continued. Add an "unclear" value for genuinely ambiguous cases. Put format normalization rules in the prompt (dates as year, month, day, currency as numbers) alongside the strict schema, to handle inconsistent source formatting.

1.title: Schema design rules, continued
1.text: Schema design rules, continued. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A field that may be missing must be nullable: a required field invites fabricated values. Exam tip: Guaranteed structure with an unknown document type means tool use with tool choice: "any" and one schema per type.

1.title: Validation, Retry and Feedback Loops
1.text: Validation, Retry and Feedback Loops. The figure shows this: Retry with error feedback: send the document, the failed extraction and the exact validation errors; do not retry when the data is simply not in the source.

1.title: Validation, Retry and Feedback Loops, continued
1.text: Validation, Retry and Feedback Loops, continued. Retry with error feedback. Send a follow-up request with the original document, the failed extraction and the specific validation errors, so the model can correct itself. When retry works. Format mismatches, structural output errors, wrong field placement. When retry does not work. The information is absent from the source (for example it lives in an external document that was not provided): another try only invites invention. Semantic validation. Check sums, ranges, cross-field rules; with Pydantic or Jason Schema plus business rules.

1.title: Validation, Retry and Feedback Loops, continued
1.text: Validation, Retry and Feedback Loops, continued. Self-correction fields. Extract calculated total next to stated total to flag discrepancies; add a conflict detected boolean when the source data is inconsistent. Feedback loop on findings. Add a detected pattern field (which construct triggered the finding) so you can analyze which patterns developers dismiss and fix false positives systematically. Exam tip: Validation failed because "the invoice does not list the shipping address anywhere"? to do not retry; accept null and route to review. Validation failed because "dates are in the wrong format"? to retry with the error message.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Structured output: Tool use plus Jason schema; read the tool use input; eliminates syntax errors. tool choice: auto may return text, any must call a tool (unknown type, several schemas), forced equals a named tool first. Not prevented: Semantic errors (totals, wrong fields) to validation code. Schema design: Optional or nullable if possibly absent, enum plus other plus detail, unclear, normalization rules in the prompt. Retry with feedback: Document plus failed output plus specific errors. Retry limits: Useless when info is absent; works for format or structure errors. Self-check: calculated total versus stated total, conflict detected, detected pattern.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A pipeline asks Claude for Jason in plain text and sometimes receives malformed output. What is the most reliable fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Tool use with a schema eliminates Jason syntax errors.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. The pipeline receives invoices, receipts and contracts, each with its own extraction tool, and the type is unknown beforehand. Claude sometimes answers in prose. Which setting is right? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. "any" guarantees a tool call while letting Claude choose the schema that matches the document.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A required purchase order field is filled with plausible but made-up numbers for invoices that have none. What is the best schema change? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. A required field pushes the model to fabricate a value; a nullable field lets it say "not present".

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. The category enum has four values, but suppliers sometimes bring new kinds of charges. How should the schema evolve? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. "other" plus a detail string keeps structure while allowing new categories.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Tool use with a strict schema produces valid Jason, yet line items do not add up to the stated total on some invoices. What does this show? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Semantic errors need extra validation, for example comparing a calculated total with the stated one.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A date field fails validation because the model returned "seven Jan two thousand twenty-six" and the schema expects year, month, day. What is the best retry? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Format errors are fixable when the model is shown exactly what failed.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Validation fails because a purchase order number is simply not in the document the pipeline has; it lives in a separate email. What should the pipeline do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Retry is ineffective when information is absent from the source.

1.title: Practice Question 8
1.text: Question eight. A team wants to understand which code patterns produce findings that developers dismiss. What should they add to the structured output? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Tracking the triggering pattern enables systematic analysis of dismissals.

1.title: Practice Question 9
1.text: Question nine. Select two. Which two schema choices reduce fabricated values? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and B. Nullable fields and an explicit unclear value give the model an honest way to answer. Required fields and forbidding null push it to invent values.

1.title: Practice Question 10
1.text: Question ten. Select two. Which two validation failures can retry-with-error-feedback realistically fix? The five options are on the screen. The answers are C and D. Format and structural mistakes can be corrected when the model sees the exact error. Absent information cannot be retried into existence.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all ten answers. Question one: C. Question two: A. Question three: D. Question four: B. Question five: A. Question six: C. Question seven: A. Question eight: D. Question nine: A and B. Question ten: C and D. In the next module, we continue the course.
